pieces.name: Voxel faces & materials
pieces.brief: Continue (read pieces/surface.md fully incl. ALL coordinator notes and the coherence.md 2026-09-27 section). The coherence pass SETTLED and froze AO (voxel bake: ao 3.8, aoDirect 4.4, aoTop [3.0,4.8] …; worldAO OFF for good) and added warm-shade chroma (shadeGain). Don't re-litigate AO strength unless 2+ consecutive critics agree AND you have ref04 profile numbers. Open: roof-deck contact pools are ~0.7 vs ref04 0.25-0.4 because the post shade-floor lifts them (an AO-aware post floor could close this), the dentil 'comb' under cornices, glass crispness (colour is already brighter than ref — don't brighten), stair-stepped parapet shadow edges at close zoom.
pieces.files: src/render/voxel.js, src/render/materials.js (not the night-only branches — night piece owns those)
pieces.judge: surface quality of buildings: face cleanliness (no grid lines/noise), colour fidelity, AO in corners/contacts, glass/material response. Compare iso-close or one-bakery against ref04 (and ref02).
history:
Wave 4 round 12: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: There is almost no contact ambient occlusion on the bakery. The inside edge where the roof parapet meets the roof deck, the undersides of the floor ledges and cornice bands, and the joint where the building meets its plinth all read flat and evenly lit. ref04 puts a soft, fairly wide dark AO gradient in every inside corner and under every overhang (quoins, sills, parapet), and that is what makes its faces feel solid and rich. Ours also has a large blank grey roof slab with no falloff toward the parapet walls, so it looks like a dead flat plane. It needs a soft darkening, about 2 to 4 voxels wide, along the base of the parapet and under each ledge and cornice.
Other notes: Faces are clean, with no grid lines or noise, and the three-tone face shading is correct. Window glass is flat blue and has too little reflection variation compared with ref02. The right-hand darkest face is fine but a bit grey-beige, where ref04's dark face has warm bounce light.

Wave 4 round 13: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: Contact and inside-corner AO is too weak on the bakery. Under the top cornice, beneath the window sills and awnings, and where the facade meets the plinth, the faces stay flat and evenly lit. The front plaza (pavers, lamp, bench area) also looks milky and washed-out, as if there is a translucent haze over it. In ref04 every ledge, quoin and inside corner casts a deep, soft occlusion gradient onto the face below, which gives the flat colours depth and warmth. Our building needs darker, wider soft AO under every overhang and at ground contacts, and the haze over the storefront paving needs to go.
Other notes: Surfaces are clean, with no grid lines or noise, and the three face tones read correctly. The right-side tan/red faces are a bit dull and grey compared with ref04's warm, saturated shadow side. The windows are a flat blue with only a small highlight, so they have little glassy reflection.

Wave 4 round 14: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: Face tones and AO. On the bakery (one-bakery, centre of frame), the left-facing and right-facing walls are nearly the same mid-tan value, so the corner reads flat. There is only a faint soft darkening under the cornice, the window ledges and the storey band. ref04 makes the right face clearly darker while keeping it a saturated orange, and it pools soft, deep occlusion into every inside corner: under each overhang, along the parapet-to-roof seam, at the quoins and where the walls meet the base. Our large light-grey roof slab is also an evenly lit, flat field with almost no occlusion gradient near the parapet walls. Darken the right face about 15-20% and keep it saturated. Strengthen and widen the contact AO under ledges and along roof edges.
Other notes: Faces are clean: no grid lines, noise or speckle. Ours has much higher detail density than ref04 (awnings, sign, window frames, rooftop props). Glass reads as blue with diagonal highlight strips, which is fine. It booted without errors on all three shots.

pieces.name: Civic, fun & deco
pieces.brief: Continue (read pieces/civic.md fully incl. ALL coordinator notes). The gallery layout is FROZEN and critics are told filler is context. Recent critics call the hero buildings strong; the gaps are: facade relief built outward (projecting cornices, proud frames, school portico, raised brick bands), roofs with structure (fire-station roof is a flat slab with identical boxes), purpose-built forecourts (striped engine apron with trucks, bus drop-off, plaza with benches/statues, pool deck), calmer small fun lots (park/playground/mini-golf/skate-park: pale paving, hedge border, 2-3 props), fire-station red with brick coursing, FISE→FIRE sign glyph.
pieces.judge: civic/fun/deco design: detail, readability, signature pieces (stadium, fire station, school, pool, monument/statue), lots — versus the corresponding buildings in ref05.
history:
Wave 4 round 12: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: The space around our civic buildings is filler. The left third of gal-fun-1 is one generic tile repeated over and over: a green plaza with benches and a small planter. The monument lot is mostly flat pale beige and grey paving, and the top right is an empty lime field. In ref05, every civic lot is filled to its kerb with distinct content: the school's courtyard garden, the monument's fountains and hedged planters, the fire station's apron with parked engines, and hospital or police bays with striped parking and vehicles. Fix: remove the repeated plaza tile from gallery or civic surroundings. Give each signature lot (monument, school, fire station, stadium) its own dense forecourt: striped parking with cars, trimmed hedge borders, small fountains and planters, and colour variety in the paving instead of plain pale concrete.
Other notes: Our hero buildings are strong and read as well as ref05's or better: the school's clock tower and portico, and the red-brick fire station with its engines. At matched tile scale our buildings are chunkier, and ref05 has more small props per tile, so ours looks lower-detail overall. The stadium (one-stadium) is close to ref05's in form, but its bowl's lower seating is a flat blue with little depth, and there is little rubble or plaza detail around its base. All shots booted with no console errors.

Wave 4 round 13: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: Lot composition around the civic buildings is too busy. In gal-fun-1, the small fun and park lots in the upper-left half and around the monument plaza are a scatter of tiny red, green and orange kiosks, hedges and props with no hierarchy, so the signature buildings don't stand out. In ref05, each civic building gets one calm lot: pale paving, a neat hedge or planter border, and a few purposeful props (ambulances in the hospital parking, fire trucks on a dark apron, fountains flanking the monument). The building silhouette dominates there. Cut the fun-lot prop count by about half, give each lot one dominant surface colour with a clear edge, and let the monument plaza be symmetric paving and water.
Other notes: 1) The fire station is a flat, oversaturated red block. The ref version has brick tone variation, cream trim and a green roof, with stronger contrast between the three faces. 2) The civic facades (school, sports club) read slightly soft next to the ref's crisp cornices, pediments and deep window reveals. The ref bank's colonnade depth in particular is not matched. 3) Strengths: the stadium in gal-fun-2 and one-stadium is a close match to ref05's stadium, the school's clock tower and portico are good, and the boot was clean with no console errors.

Wave 4 round 14: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: Our civic buildings don't have the reference's fine detail. The school's facade (upper center) is mostly big flat cream and teal faces with widely spaced, repeated window modules. The fire station's roof (right) is covered in a grid of identical grey boxes. In ref05, the town hall, monument and fire station are packed with fine mullions, pilasters, cornice trim, statues and varied rooftop kit, and each sits on a compact, framed forecourt lot. Ours need finer facade articulation, varied rooftop equipment instead of a repeated box grid, and tighter forecourt lots.
Other notes: The shots booted with no console errors in gal-fun-1/2/3, gal-deco-1 or one-stadium (the one-school result line wasn't checked). Ours is brighter, cleaner and more cheerful than the reference, and the stadium in gal-fun-2 compares well with ref05's. The filler plazas and fountains take up a lot of our frame, which weakens the civic focus. Our buildings sit at about 3x the reference scale, so I downscaled our frame to match.

pieces.name: Houses & apartments
pieces.brief: Continue (read pieces/res.md fully incl. ALL coordinator notes). Gallery layout is FROZEN (flower-bed plots between houses). Shading (AO, warm shade chroma) was settled globally by the coherence pass — not yours. Your consistent gap (r7-r14): SIMPLIFY — one smooth wall colour per face, ONE crisp frame per window, chunky single-tone quoins (no striped banding), one clear door with two wall lamps, a legible rooftop room/AC box (not oversized quoins crowding the roof), clean warm cream roof deck, terracotta walls (keep). Then apply the same calm treatment to the other house ids.
pieces.files: src/models/residential.js (+ your palette block in core.js)
pieces.judge: residential design vs houses in ref04, ref05, ref01.
history:
Wave 4 round 12: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: In the one-small-house shot, the orange stucco walls show blotchy, smeared darker-orange gradients. It's worst on the right-hand shaded facade around the upper windows, where the facade meets the roof parapet, and at the base of the penthouse. The reference (ref04) keeps every face one clean, even colour, with only a thin soft AO band in the inside corners and under ledges. Remove the diffuse wall-darkening or shadow leak so each facade reads as one confident tone, and keep AO tight to the corners.
Other notes: No console errors on any of the 4 shots. The ref04 pair was a close-up of the small house; ours had lot and street context the reference lacks, and still lost on surface cleanliness. In ours, the sandstone quoins around the windows are chunkier and busier than ref04's evenly stepped quoins, and the red door mat and planters sit in a crowded, flat-lit forecourt. gal-homes-1 is strong on variety, roofs and lot dressing, but the cluster is very dense and the roof tile stripes read slightly noisy.

Wave 4 round 13: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: The small house's lighting and material depth fall short of ref04. Our wall faces are flat single tones. The undersides of the cornice and quoin blocks and the corners where the rooftop cabin meets the roof get almost no soft contact darkening (AO), so the house looks slightly pasted-on and washed out. Ref04 has a pronounced soft AO falloff in every inside corner and under every overhang, plus a gentle warm gradient down each wall face that separates top, left and right faces richly. Our lot's side band is also a near-black slab (bottom right of the house), which competes with the building. It should be a lighter concrete tone. Fix: stronger, wider AO on the building models themselves (cornice undersides, quoins, roof-to-wall joins) and a subtle vertical gradient on the wall faces.
Other notes: No console errors, and all 4 shots rendered. gal-homes-1 is strong on detail density (dormers, balconies, gardens, parked cars) and roughly on a par with ref05's density; the loss here is on material and lighting quality, not on content. The edges of the voxels on our house look slightly soft next to ref04's crisp bevels, and the right-hand walls lean muddy orange-brown.

Wave 4 round 14: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: Ours has almost no soft ambient occlusion in inside corners. On one-small-house, the joins where the walls meet the roof deck, the base of the penthouse, the door recess, the planter bases and the wall-to-lot seam all stay a single flat tone. In ref04 each of those corners gets a soft, darker gradient, which makes the house look solid and planted on its lot. Ours looks like stacked boxes pasted onto a slab. Fix: add contact/corner AO darkening of about 15-25%, spread over 2-4 voxels, at every concave join. Also shrink the penthouse corner quoins: they are oversized, crowd the roof deck, and swamp the penthouse door and AC unit.
Other notes: Ours has more detail and context than ref04: two floors, lit glass, flower boxes, a street lamp, and a lot plinth with a rim. The window glass reflections are good. The gal-homes-1 street block is lively and on-palette. The game booted with no console errors.

pieces.name: Downtown towers
pieces.brief: Continue (read pieces/downtown.md fully incl. ALL coordinator notes). 22 wave-4 losses converge on: (1) towers crowd each other — each tower on its own clearly bounded, paved lot with a forecourt/porte-cochere, footprint ≤60% of lot, no parked cars on tower lots; (2) facade depth built OUTWARD (proud pilasters, cornices, heavier podium) with a composed base/shaft/crown and floors that are not all identical; (3) glass palette: pane bodies dtGlass/dtGlassTeal with dtGlassHi highlights, Deep/Dark only for reveals; (4) per-id identity (material family, crown, rooftop kit). The gallery context (ring of low shops/homes) is frozen.
pieces.judge: tower/office design: facade articulation, glass, entrances, rooftops, silhouette variety, lots — versus the bank/hotel/hospital/tower in ref05.
history:
Wave 4 round 12: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: Our tower shafts (SPIRE, TWINS and the blue-grey slab behind BANK in gal-downtown-3) repeat one identical window-and-pier grid for 10+ floors, and the towers are packed so tightly that their lots barely read. In ref05, the bank, hospital and hotel each have a distinct composed facade (fluted colonnade, glass curtain bays, a stepped podium with an entrance canopy) on a clearly bounded lot with its own parking or plaza. Fix: split each shaft into base, middle and crown, change the bay rhythm between them, add recessed glass bands and setback terraces, and give each tower visible forecourt paving and parking.
Other notes: The one-glass-skyscraper and iso-mid shots never finished inside the time limit, so the pair uses a crop of gal-downtown-3 (3200x1800, crop x760,y240, 2130x1330) against ref05 (x790,y300, 1120x700). No console errors on the three gallery shots. Our tower silhouettes are a strength: spire antenna, twin crowns, clock-pediment bank and signage all read well and are more vertical than ref05. Next to ref05's crisp detail, ours looks chunkier and busier, and the filler shops and homes pressing on the tower lots add visual noise.

Wave 4 round 13: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: The downtown towers (TWINS, SPIRE, BANK and the grey glass tower in gal-downtown-3) stand shoulder to shoulder with almost no visible lot. Their bases are swallowed by neighbouring buildings and parked cars. Their tan and grey facades read as flat horizontal banding with shallow windows. ref05's bank and hotel each sit alone on a generous paved plinth with a light rim, an entrance canopy, planters and hedges. Their facades are cut deep, with recessed dark-glass windows, bold pilasters and columns, and reflective blue panes that catch highlights. To fix: widen and show each tower's forecourt lot, recess the windows 1-2 voxels behind the piers so each window gets a strong shadow edge, and give the glass bands a brighter blue with a highlight.
Other notes: A stray white voxel block floats on the TWINS tower facade (right of centre, around 1:3 height). At ref05 scale the towers fill the whole frame and are cut off, so the silhouettes lose clarity. The rooftop crowns (stepped gold spires, antenna) are good and are ours' strongest point. Renders booted cleanly with no console errors.

Wave 4 round 14: critic picked the REFERENCE.
Biggest gap: Our tower glass and facades are the biggest gap. On the TECH tower, the blue-grey office tower behind it and the pale BANK front, the glass reads as matte, dark punched holes in flat panels. In ref05 the bank, hotel and hospital glass is bright sky-blue with diagonal white reflection streaks inside crisp light frames, and it is the main thing that makes those buildings sparkle. Our towers also stand shoulder to shoulder, overlapping each other, so each one's lot, forecourt and entrance are hidden. The reference instead puts each building on its own open plinth with a visible paved forecourt, steps and planters.
Other notes: Our silhouettes vary well: twin spires, a clock-tower bank, stepped setbacks and a helipad hotel. The bank's large light-grey faces lose the three-tone separation, so the left and right faces look alike and washed out. The iso-mid shot was still rendering when judged, so the pair used a crop of gal-downtown-3 (1920x1280 crop against a 1000x667 ref05 crop of the bank/hotel region).
